# 54 Hermes as a first-class Dora provider

_Research · 2026-08-31 · Exa + local CLI + official docs. Research only. Does not change product code._

**Question:** What Hermes commands and flags does Dora actually have to speak, now that Hermes is the night-pass runtime?

**Pinned binary:** local Hermes Agent **v0.20.6** (2026.8.27), upstream `38b7d0f4`, install `/Users/saif/.hermes/hermes-agent`. Six commits behind at capture time. Official pages: [CLI commands](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands), [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [MCP](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp), [MCP config](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference), [tools](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tools), [cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts`, `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`. Spec: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

---

## Mental model

Hermes is the agent. Dora is the front desk.

| Role | Owner |
|------|--------|
| Grill, write `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`, print next line | Dora |
| Interactive chat, one-shot, cron ticker, MCP OAuth, gateway | Hermes |
| Scalekit tools | Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP, named `scalekit` in Hermes |

Dora must call only flags Hermes accepts. A wrong flag is a user-visible crash. That already happened: `cron create --toolsets … --timeout …` → `unrecognized arguments`.

Do not treat official docs and local `--help` as the same surface. Docs describe post-0.21 `hermes chat --oneshot -q`. Local 0.20.6 still uses top-level `-z` / `--oneshot PROMPT` (the next token is the prompt).

---

## What Dora already calls

From `bootArgs` / `onePassArgs` / `pauseArgs` / `resumeArgs` / `listJobStates` (working tree after the flag fix, not yet committed at research time):

| Dora verb | Hermes argv | Status vs v0.20.6 `--help` |
|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
| `harness new --run-one-pass` | `hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot <prompt>` | **Valid.** `-t` / `--toolsets` applies to `-z` / `--oneshot` and `--tui` only. `--oneshot` consumes the next token. Flags must come first. |
| `harness boot` step 1 | `hermes gateway install` | **Valid.** Writes launchd (macOS) or systemd (Linux). Does not start a chat. |
| `harness boot` step 2 | `hermes mcp add scalekit --url <url> --auth oauth` | **Valid syntax.** Does **not** finish OAuth. |
| `harness boot` step 3 | `hermes cron create every <interval> <prompt> --name <slug> [--skill …]` | **Valid.** No `--toolsets`. No `--timeout`. |
| `harness pause <slug>` | `hermes cron pause <slug>` | **Valid.** Job-level. Leaves the gateway up. |
| `harness resume <slug>` | `hermes cron resume <slug>` | **Valid.** Recalculates next future run. |
| `harness list` | `hermes cron list` then parse `[active]` / `[paused]` | **Fragile.** Official list also uses `[completed]`. Empty list is prose, not a table. |

Not called today: `mcp login`, `mcp test`, `tools enable --platform cron`, `cron run`, `cron edit`, `cron remove`, `cron status`, `gateway start` / `status`, `hermes doctor`.

`hermesTimeoutSec(maxTick)` is still exported and tested. Boot and one-pass do **not** pass it. Spec story 21 (max tick 10m) is not wired to a Hermes flag.

---

## Flag contract (the part that already bit us)

### One-shot (the grill test pass)

Local v0.20.6, from `hermes --help`:

```
-z PROMPT, --oneshot PROMPT
    One-shot mode: send a single prompt and print ONLY the final
    response text to stdout. … Tools, memory, rules, and AGENTS.md
    in the CWD are loaded as normal; approvals are auto-bypassed.
-t TOOLSETS, --toolsets TOOLSETS
    Comma-separated toolsets. Applies to -z/--oneshot and --tui.
```

Correct order:

```bash
hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot "the prompt text"
```

Wrong (the live crash):

```bash
hermes cron create "every 1h" "…" --toolsets mcp-scalekit --timeout 600
hermes --oneshot --toolsets mcp-scalekit "…"   # --oneshot eats --toolsets
```

Official CLI page (newer than 0.20.6) prefers:

```bash
hermes chat --oneshot -q "…"
hermes chat --query-file prompt.md --oneshot
```

`chat --query-file` is safer for long unattended prompts (quotes, `$(…)`, backticks arrive verbatim). Dora currently puts the whole prompt on argv.

`hermes chat` also has `--run-budget SECONDS` (wall-clock wrap-up). That is the closest one-pass match for routine `maxTick`. Top-level `-z` on 0.20.6 has **no** `--timeout` and **no** `--run-budget`.

### Cron create (the night job)

Local `hermes cron create --help` accepts:

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `schedule` (positional) | `30m`, `every 2h`, `0 9 * * *` |
| `prompt` (positional, optional) | Task text |
| `--name` | Human name. Dora uses the slug. Pause/resume/list key off this. |
| `--skill` (repeatable) | Attach a skill |
| `--workdir` | Absolute cwd. Loads `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules`. Omit = no project files. |
| `--model` / `--provider` | User-owned pin. The agent `cronjob` tool cannot set this. |
| `--reasoning-effort` | `none` … `ultra` |
| `--deliver` | `origin`, `local`, telegram, discord, … Spec says do not bake Slack/Discord into the harness. |
| `--script` / `--no-agent` | Script-only job. Not our path. |
| `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url` | Cheap hash gate before the LLM. |
| `--continuity` | Inject previous run output into the next prompt. |
| `--repeat` | Finite count |

**Not on the parser:** `--toolsets`, `--timeout`, `-t`, `--oneshot`. [Issue #24134](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/24134) asked for `--toolsets` on create (v0.13.0). Still open. PR #24145 referenced, not the supported surface.

Schedule without `every` or `*`: Hermes treats a bare `30m` / `1d` as a **one-shot**, then the job goes `[completed]`. Dora wraps with `hermesSchedule()` → `every 1h`. Keep that.

---

## Cron toolsets (how Scalekit actually reaches the night job)

Cron does **not** inherit CLI `--toolsets`.

Resolution order (official cron page + GitHub #23997 / commit `74a5905`):

1. Per-job `enabled_toolsets` on the `cronjob` **tool** (not the CLI).
2. Else the **`cron` platform** list from `hermes tools`.
3. Else defaults.
4. MCP servers are then layered on, **if** they are named as `mcp-<server>` (or the platform list includes them).

The internal alias for an MCP server named `scalekit` is **`mcp-scalekit`**. That is why one-pass uses `--toolsets mcp-scalekit`.

Known footguns:

| You write | What happens |
|-----------|----------------|
| `hermes tools enable scalekit --platform cron` | CLI may accept it. Cron validation can drop it. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["scalekit"]` or `["scalekit:*"]` or `["mcp:scalekit"]` | Silent drop on older builds. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["mcp-scalekit"]` | Registers. |
| `hermes tools enable mcp-scalekit --platform cron` | Correct CLI form. |
| Per-job list of only native toolsets (`web`, `terminal`) | Older scheduler returned that list verbatim and **stripped all MCP**. Later fix unions globally-enabled MCP back in (`74a5905`, issue #23997). Do not assume every install has this. |

Cron also **disables** `cronjob`, `messaging`, and `clarify` so a night job cannot spawn more cron or prompt a human ([cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting)).

One-shot and cron are different MCP discovery paths. `-z` has historically snapshotted tools **before** MCP discovery ([#38448](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/38448)). Slow HTTP OAuth MCP can miss the first (only) turn. `hermes mcp test scalekit` can pass while `-z` has no `mcp_scalekit_*` tools. If one-pass “works” without calling Scalekit, this is the first place to look.

**First-class implication:** boot must do more than `mcp add`. It must also put `mcp-scalekit` on the **cron** platform (or write `enabled_toolsets` in `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`). CLI `cron create` cannot set that list.

---

## MCP add and OAuth

Local `hermes mcp add --help`:

```
hermes mcp add <name> --url URL [--auth {oauth,header}]
hermes mcp add <name> --command CMD --args …
```

`--auth oauth` writes `auth: oauth` under `mcp_servers.<name>` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Tokens live in `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<name>.json` (mode 0600), not in config.

OAuth is **not** finished by `mcp add`. Official MCP page and `hermes mcp login --help`:

```bash
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

First connect: discover OAuth metadata, optional dynamic client registration, open a browser, wait on loopback. `mcp add` from Dora is `spawnSync` with pipes. There is no TTY and no 5-minute wait. Boot can write the config row and still leave an unauthenticated server.

`hermes mcp login` is the explicit re-auth path. Dora does not run it. That is a product hole, not a Hermes bug.

Do not use `hermes mcp install` / catalog for Scalekit. Catalog is Nous-approved third-party servers.

`mcp add` is discovery-first. It may probe the URL. A fake URL (`https://example.invalid/mcp`) can fail add even when the flag parse is correct.

## Timeouts (spec max tick)

Two different clocks. Do not mix them.

| Knob | What it limits | Default | Dora today |
|------|----------------|---------|------------|
| `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT` | **Idle** time with no tool call / token stream. `0` = unlimited. Job may run for hours if it keeps working. | 600s | Not set. `hermesTimeoutSec("10m")` equals 600 but is unused. |
| `cron.script_timeout_seconds` / `HERMES_CRON_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` | Pre-run **script** only | 3600s | N/A (we are not `--script`) |
| `hermes chat --run-budget SECONDS` | Wall-clock for a conversation run. 80% wrap-up notice. | off | Not used |
| Top-level `-z` | No timeout flag | — | Current one-pass |

Spec story 21 (“stuck pass cannot run forever”) is **not** the Hermes idle timeout. A busy agent ignores `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`. A wall-clock cap needs `--run-budget` on `chat`, or a Hermes config we do not set today.

## Gateway, sleep, pause

Cron fires only if the **gateway ticker** is alive. A CLI chat does not tick cron. Tick is every 60s.

```bash
hermes gateway install   # Dora boot. launchd/systemd unit.
hermes gateway start     # Start the installed service. Boot does not call this.
hermes gateway status    # Live: launchd PID 77189, service matches install.
hermes cron status       # Live: “Gateway is running — cron jobs will fire automatically.”
```

`gateway install` writes the unit. It is not a guarantee the process is up on this boot. First-class boot should `status` (or `start`) after install.

`hermes pause` (no `cron`) is a **global emergency stop**: new cron dispatch, kanban dispatch, new gateway turns. In-flight work is not killed. This is not `dora harness pause`. Do not call it.

Laptop close is host sleep. The ticker stops. Due jobs may fire on wake if the job is still `[active]`. That matches spec stories 33–35. Hermes has no “pause because the lid closed.”

Local v0.20.6, from `hermes --help`:


```bash
hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot "the prompt text"
```

```bash
hermes cron create "every 1h" "…" --toolsets mcp-scalekit --timeout 600
```

**Question:** What Hermes commands and flags does Dora actually have to speak, now that Hermes is the night-pass runtime?

**Pinned binary:** local Hermes Agent **v0.20.6** (2026.8.27), upstream `38b7d0f4`, install `/Users/saif/.hermes/hermes-agent`. Six commits behind at capture time. Official pages: [CLI commands](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands), [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [MCP](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp), [MCP config](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference), [tools](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tools), [cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts`, `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`. Spec: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

---

## Mental model

Hermes is the agent. Dora is the front desk.

| Role | Owner |
|------|--------|
| Grill, write `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`, print next line | Dora |
| Interactive chat, one-shot, cron ticker, MCP OAuth, gateway | Hermes |
| Scalekit tools | Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP, named `scalekit` in Hermes |

Dora must call only flags Hermes accepts. A wrong flag is a user-visible crash. That already happened: `cron create --toolsets … --timeout …` → `unrecognized arguments`.

Do not treat official docs and local `--help` as the same surface. Docs describe post-0.21 `hermes chat --oneshot -q`. Local 0.20.6 still uses top-level `-z` / `--oneshot PROMPT` (the next token is the prompt).

---

## What Dora already calls

From `bootArgs` / `onePassArgs` / `pauseArgs` / `resumeArgs` / `listJobStates` (working tree after the flag fix, not yet committed at research time):

| Dora verb | Hermes argv | Status vs v0.20.6 `--help` |
|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
| `harness new --run-one-pass` | `hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot <prompt>` | **Valid.** `-t` / `--toolsets` applies to `-z` / `--oneshot` and `--tui` only. `--oneshot` consumes the next token. Flags must come first. |
| `harness boot` step 1 | `hermes gateway install` | **Valid.** Writes launchd (macOS) or systemd (Linux). Does not start a chat. |
| `harness boot` step 2 | `hermes mcp add scalekit --url <url> --auth oauth` | **Valid syntax.** Does **not** finish OAuth. |
| `harness boot` step 3 | `hermes cron create every <interval> <prompt> --name <slug> [--skill …]` | **Valid.** No `--toolsets`. No `--timeout`. |
| `harness pause <slug>` | `hermes cron pause <slug>` | **Valid.** Job-level. Leaves the gateway up. |
| `harness resume <slug>` | `hermes cron resume <slug>` | **Valid.** Recalculates next future run. |
| `harness list` | `hermes cron list` then parse `[active]` / `[paused]` | **Fragile.** Official list also uses `[completed]`. Empty list is prose, not a table. |

Not called today: `mcp login`, `mcp test`, `tools enable --platform cron`, `cron run`, `cron edit`, `cron remove`, `cron status`, `gateway start` / `status`, `hermes doctor`.

`hermesTimeoutSec(maxTick)` is still exported and tested. Boot and one-pass do **not** pass it. Spec story 21 (max tick 10m) is not wired to a Hermes flag.

---

## Flag contract (the part that already bit us)

### One-shot (the grill test pass)

Local v0.20.6, from `hermes --help`:

```
-z PROMPT, --oneshot PROMPT
    One-shot mode: send a single prompt and print ONLY the final
    response text to stdout. … Tools, memory, rules, and AGENTS.md
    in the CWD are loaded as normal; approvals are auto-bypassed.
-t TOOLSETS, --toolsets TOOLSETS
    Comma-separated toolsets. Applies to -z/--oneshot and --tui.
```

Correct order:

```bash
hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot "the prompt text"
```

Wrong (the live crash):

```bash
hermes cron create "every 1h" "…" --toolsets mcp-scalekit --timeout 600
hermes --oneshot --toolsets mcp-scalekit "…"   # --oneshot eats --toolsets
```

Official CLI page (newer than 0.20.6) prefers:

```bash
hermes chat --oneshot -q "…"
hermes chat --query-file prompt.md --oneshot
```

`chat --query-file` is safer for long unattended prompts (quotes, `$(…)`, backticks arrive verbatim). Dora currently puts the whole prompt on argv.

`hermes chat` also has `--run-budget SECONDS` (wall-clock wrap-up). That is the closest one-pass match for routine `maxTick`. Top-level `-z` on 0.20.6 has **no** `--timeout` and **no** `--run-budget`.

### Cron create (the night job)

Local `hermes cron create --help` accepts:

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `schedule` (positional) | `30m`, `every 2h`, `0 9 * * *` |
| `prompt` (positional, optional) | Task text |
| `--name` | Human name. Dora uses the slug. Pause/resume/list key off this. |
| `--skill` (repeatable) | Attach a skill |
| `--workdir` | Absolute cwd. Loads `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules`. Omit = no project files. |
| `--model` / `--provider` | User-owned pin. The agent `cronjob` tool cannot set this. |
| `--reasoning-effort` | `none` … `ultra` |
| `--deliver` | `origin`, `local`, telegram, discord, … Spec says do not bake Slack/Discord into the harness. |
| `--script` / `--no-agent` | Script-only job. Not our path. |
| `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url` | Cheap hash gate before the LLM. |
| `--continuity` | Inject previous run output into the next prompt. |
| `--repeat` | Finite count |

**Not on the parser:** `--toolsets`, `--timeout`, `-t`, `--oneshot`. [Issue #24134](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/24134) asked for `--toolsets` on create (v0.13.0). Still open. PR #24145 referenced, not the supported surface.

Schedule without `every` or `*`: Hermes treats a bare `30m` / `1d` as a **one-shot**, then the job goes `[completed]`. Dora wraps with `hermesSchedule()` → `every 1h`. Keep that.

---

## Cron toolsets (how Scalekit actually reaches the night job)

Cron does **not** inherit CLI `--toolsets`.

Resolution order (official cron page + GitHub #23997 / commit `74a5905`):

1. Per-job `enabled_toolsets` on the `cronjob` **tool** (not the CLI).
2. Else the **`cron` platform** list from `hermes tools`.
3. Else defaults.
4. MCP servers are then layered on, **if** they are named as `mcp-<server>` (or the platform list includes them).

The internal alias for an MCP server named `scalekit` is **`mcp-scalekit`**. That is why one-pass uses `--toolsets mcp-scalekit`.

Known footguns:

| You write | What happens |
|-----------|----------------|
| `hermes tools enable scalekit --platform cron` | CLI may accept it. Cron validation can drop it. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["scalekit"]` or `["scalekit:*"]` or `["mcp:scalekit"]` | Silent drop on older builds. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["mcp-scalekit"]` | Registers. |
| `hermes tools enable mcp-scalekit --platform cron` | Correct CLI form. |
| Per-job list of only native toolsets (`web`, `terminal`) | Older scheduler returned that list verbatim and **stripped all MCP**. Later fix unions globally-enabled MCP back in (`74a5905`, issue #23997). Do not assume every install has this. |

Cron also **disables** `cronjob`, `messaging`, and `clarify` so a night job cannot spawn more cron or prompt a human ([cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting)).

One-shot and cron are different MCP discovery paths. `-z` has historically snapshotted tools **before** MCP discovery ([#38448](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/38448)). Slow HTTP OAuth MCP can miss the first (only) turn. `hermes mcp test scalekit` can pass while `-z` has no `mcp_scalekit_*` tools. If one-pass “works” without calling Scalekit, this is the first place to look.

**First-class implication:** boot must do more than `mcp add`. It must also put `mcp-scalekit` on the **cron** platform (or write `enabled_toolsets` in `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`). CLI `cron create` cannot set that list.

Local `hermes mcp add --help`:

```
hermes mcp add <name> --url URL [--auth {oauth,header}]
hermes mcp add <name> --command CMD --args …
```

`--auth oauth` writes `auth: oauth` under `mcp_servers.<name>` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Tokens live in `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<name>.json` (mode 0600), not in config.

OAuth is **not** finished by `mcp add`. Official MCP page and `hermes mcp login --help`:

```bash
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

First connect: discover OAuth metadata, optional dynamic client registration, open a browser, wait on loopback. `mcp add` from Dora is `spawnSync` with pipes. There is no TTY and no 5-minute wait. Boot can write the config row and still leave an unauthenticated server.

`hermes mcp login` is the explicit re-auth path. Dora does not run it. That is a product hole, not a Hermes bug.

Related MCP verbs Dora may want later:

| Command | Use |
|---------|-----|
| `hermes mcp list` | Confirm `scalekit` exists. Empty today on this machine. |
| `hermes mcp test scalekit` | Reachability after login. |
| `hermes mcp configure scalekit` | Tool include/exclude checklist. Interactive. |
| `hermes mcp remove scalekit` | Unboot / replace URL. |
| `hermes mcp reauth --all` | Fleet refresh. |

Do not use `hermes mcp install` / catalog for Scalekit. Catalog is Nous-approved third-party servers.

`mcp add` is discovery-first. It may probe the URL. A fake URL (`https://example.invalid/mcp`) can fail add even when the flag parse is correct.

## Timeouts (spec max tick)

Two different clocks. Do not mix them.

| Knob | What it limits | Default | Dora today |
|------|----------------|---------|------------|
| `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT` | **Idle** time with no tool call / token stream. `0` = unlimited. Job may run for hours if it keeps working. | 600s | Not set. `hermesTimeoutSec("10m")` equals 600 but is unused. |
| `cron.script_timeout_seconds` / `HERMES_CRON_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` | Pre-run **script** only | 3600s | N/A (we are not `--script`) |
| `hermes chat --run-budget SECONDS` | Wall-clock for a conversation run. 80% wrap-up notice. | off | Not used |
| Top-level `-z` | No timeout flag | — | Current one-pass |

Spec story 21 (“stuck pass cannot run forever”) is **not** the Hermes idle timeout. A busy agent ignores `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`. A wall-clock cap needs `--run-budget` on `chat`, or a Hermes config we do not set today.

Cron fires only if the **gateway ticker** is alive. A CLI chat does not tick cron. Tick is every 60s.

```bash

hermes gateway start     # Start the installed service. Boot does not call this.
hermes gateway status    # Live: launchd PID 77189, service matches install.
hermes cron status       # Live: “Gateway is running — cron jobs will fire automatically.”
```

`hermes pause` (no `cron`) is a **global emergency stop**: new cron dispatch, kanban dispatch, new gateway turns. In-flight work is not killed. This is not `dora harness pause`. Do not call it.

Official pages: [CLI commands](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands), [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [MCP](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp), [MCP config](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference), [tools](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tools), [cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts`, `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`. Spec: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

---

## Mental model

Hermes is the agent. Dora is the front desk.

| Role | Owner |
|------|--------|
| Grill, write `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`, print next line | Dora |
| Interactive chat, one-shot, cron ticker, MCP OAuth, gateway | Hermes |
| Scalekit tools | Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP, named `scalekit` in Hermes |

Dora must call only flags Hermes accepts. A wrong flag is a user-visible crash. That already happened: `cron create --toolsets … --timeout …` → `unrecognized arguments`.

Do not treat official docs and local `--help` as the same surface. Docs describe post-0.21 `hermes chat --oneshot -q`. Local 0.20.6 still uses top-level `-z` / `--oneshot PROMPT` (the next token is the prompt).

---

## What Dora already calls

From `bootArgs` / `onePassArgs` / `pauseArgs` / `resumeArgs` / `listJobStates` (working tree after the flag fix, not yet committed at research time):

| Dora verb | Hermes argv | Status vs v0.20.6 `--help` |
|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
| `harness new --run-one-pass` | `hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot <prompt>` | **Valid.** `-t` / `--toolsets` applies to `-z` / `--oneshot` and `--tui` only. `--oneshot` consumes the next token. Flags must come first. |
| `harness boot` step 1 | `hermes gateway install` | **Valid.** Writes launchd (macOS) or systemd (Linux). Does not start a chat. |
| `harness boot` step 2 | `hermes mcp add scalekit --url <url> --auth oauth` | **Valid syntax.** Does **not** finish OAuth. |
| `harness boot` step 3 | `hermes cron create every <interval> <prompt> --name <slug> [--skill …]` | **Valid.** No `--toolsets`. No `--timeout`. |
| `harness pause <slug>` | `hermes cron pause <slug>` | **Valid.** Job-level. Leaves the gateway up. |
| `harness resume <slug>` | `hermes cron resume <slug>` | **Valid.** Recalculates next future run. |
| `harness list` | `hermes cron list` then parse `[active]` / `[paused]` | **Fragile.** Official list also uses `[completed]`. Empty list is prose, not a table. |

Not called today: `mcp login`, `mcp test`, `tools enable --platform cron`, `cron run`, `cron edit`, `cron remove`, `cron status`, `gateway start` / `status`, `hermes doctor`.

`hermesTimeoutSec(maxTick)` is still exported and tested. Boot and one-pass do **not** pass it. Spec story 21 (max tick 10m) is not wired to a Hermes flag.

---

## Flag contract (the part that already bit us)

### One-shot (the grill test pass)

Local v0.20.6, from `hermes --help`:

```
-z PROMPT, --oneshot PROMPT
    One-shot mode: send a single prompt and print ONLY the final
    response text to stdout. … Tools, memory, rules, and AGENTS.md
    in the CWD are loaded as normal; approvals are auto-bypassed.
-t TOOLSETS, --toolsets TOOLSETS
    Comma-separated toolsets. Applies to -z/--oneshot and --tui.
```

Correct order:

```bash
hermes --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot "the prompt text"
```

Wrong (the live crash):

```bash
hermes cron create "every 1h" "…" --toolsets mcp-scalekit --timeout 600
hermes --oneshot --toolsets mcp-scalekit "…"   # --oneshot eats --toolsets
```

Official CLI page (newer than 0.20.6) prefers:

```bash
hermes chat --oneshot -q "…"
hermes chat --query-file prompt.md --oneshot
```

`chat --query-file` is safer for long unattended prompts (quotes, `$(…)`, backticks arrive verbatim). Dora currently puts the whole prompt on argv.

`hermes chat` also has `--run-budget SECONDS` (wall-clock wrap-up). That is the closest one-pass match for routine `maxTick`. Top-level `-z` on 0.20.6 has **no** `--timeout` and **no** `--run-budget`.

### Cron create (the night job)

Local `hermes cron create --help` accepts:

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `schedule` (positional) | `30m`, `every 2h`, `0 9 * * *` |
| `prompt` (positional, optional) | Task text |
| `--name` | Human name. Dora uses the slug. Pause/resume/list key off this. |
| `--skill` (repeatable) | Attach a skill |
| `--workdir` | Absolute cwd. Loads `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules`. Omit = no project files. |
| `--model` / `--provider` | User-owned pin. The agent `cronjob` tool cannot set this. |
| `--reasoning-effort` | `none` … `ultra` |
| `--deliver` | `origin`, `local`, telegram, discord, … Spec says do not bake Slack/Discord into the harness. |
| `--script` / `--no-agent` | Script-only job. Not our path. |
| `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url` | Cheap hash gate before the LLM. |
| `--continuity` | Inject previous run output into the next prompt. |
| `--repeat` | Finite count |

**Not on the parser:** `--toolsets`, `--timeout`, `-t`, `--oneshot`. [Issue #24134](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/24134) asked for `--toolsets` on create (v0.13.0). Still open. PR #24145 referenced, not the supported surface.

Schedule without `every` or `*`: Hermes treats a bare `30m` / `1d` as a **one-shot**, then the job goes `[completed]`. Dora wraps with `hermesSchedule()` → `every 1h`. Keep that.

---

## Cron toolsets (how Scalekit actually reaches the night job)

Cron does **not** inherit CLI `--toolsets`.

Resolution order (official cron page + GitHub #23997 / commit `74a5905`):

1. Per-job `enabled_toolsets` on the `cronjob` **tool** (not the CLI).
2. Else the **`cron` platform** list from `hermes tools`.
3. Else defaults.
4. MCP servers are then layered on, **if** they are named as `mcp-<server>` (or the platform list includes them).

The internal alias for an MCP server named `scalekit` is **`mcp-scalekit`**. That is why one-pass uses `--toolsets mcp-scalekit`.

Known footguns:

| You write | What happens |
|-----------|----------------|
| `hermes tools enable scalekit --platform cron` | CLI may accept it. Cron validation can drop it. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["scalekit"]` or `["scalekit:*"]` or `["mcp:scalekit"]` | Silent drop on older builds. |
| `enabled_toolsets: ["mcp-scalekit"]` | Registers. |
| `hermes tools enable mcp-scalekit --platform cron` | Correct CLI form. |
| Per-job list of only native toolsets (`web`, `terminal`) | Older scheduler returned that list verbatim and **stripped all MCP**. Later fix unions globally-enabled MCP back in (`74a5905`, issue #23997). Do not assume every install has this. |

Cron also **disables** `cronjob`, `messaging`, and `clarify` so a night job cannot spawn more cron or prompt a human ([cron troubleshooting](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/cron-troubleshooting)).

One-shot and cron are different MCP discovery paths. `-z` has historically snapshotted tools **before** MCP discovery ([#38448](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/38448)). Slow HTTP OAuth MCP can miss the first (only) turn. `hermes mcp test scalekit` can pass while `-z` has no `mcp_scalekit_*` tools. If one-pass “works” without calling Scalekit, this is the first place to look.

**First-class implication:** boot must do more than `mcp add`. It must also put `mcp-scalekit` on the **cron** platform (or write `enabled_toolsets` in `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`). CLI `cron create` cannot set that list.

---

## MCP add and OAuth

Local `hermes mcp add --help`:

```
hermes mcp add <name> --url URL [--auth {oauth,header}]
hermes mcp add <name> --command CMD --args …
```

`--auth oauth` writes `auth: oauth` under `mcp_servers.<name>` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Tokens live in `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<name>.json` (mode 0600), not in config.

OAuth is **not** finished by `mcp add`. Official MCP page and `hermes mcp login --help`:

```bash
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

First connect: discover OAuth metadata, optional dynamic client registration, open a browser, wait on loopback. `mcp add` from Dora is `spawnSync` with pipes. There is no TTY and no 5-minute wait. Boot can write the config row and still leave an unauthenticated server.

`hermes mcp login` is the explicit re-auth path. Dora does not run it. That is a product hole, not a Hermes bug.

Related MCP verbs Dora may want later:

| Command | Use |
|---------|-----|
| `hermes mcp list` | Confirm `scalekit` exists. Empty today on this machine. |
| `hermes mcp test scalekit` | Reachability after login. |
| `hermes mcp configure scalekit` | Tool include/exclude checklist. Interactive. |
| `hermes mcp remove scalekit` | Unboot / replace URL. |
| `hermes mcp reauth --all` | Fleet refresh. |

Do not use `hermes mcp install` / catalog for Scalekit. Catalog is Nous-approved third-party servers.

`mcp add` is discovery-first. It may probe the URL. A fake URL (`https://example.invalid/mcp`) can fail add even when the flag parse is correct.

---

## Timeouts (spec max tick)

Two different clocks. Do not mix them.

| Knob | What it limits | Default | Dora today |
|------|----------------|---------|------------|
| `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT` | **Idle** time with no tool call / token stream. `0` = unlimited. Job may run for hours if it keeps working. | 600s | Not set. `hermesTimeoutSec("10m")` equals 600 but is unused. |
| `cron.script_timeout_seconds` / `HERMES_CRON_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` | Pre-run **script** only | 3600s | N/A (we are not `--script`) |
| `hermes chat --run-budget SECONDS` | Wall-clock for a conversation run. 80% wrap-up notice. | off | Not used |
| Top-level `-z` | No timeout flag | — | Current one-pass |

Spec story 21 (“stuck pass cannot run forever”) is **not** the Hermes idle timeout. A busy agent ignores `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`. A wall-clock cap needs `--run-budget` on `chat`, or a Hermes config we do not set today.

---

## Gateway, sleep, pause

Cron fires only if the **gateway ticker** is alive. A CLI chat does not tick cron. Tick is every 60s.

```bash
hermes gateway install   # Dora boot. launchd/systemd unit.
hermes gateway start     # Start the installed service. Boot does not call this.
hermes gateway status    # Live: launchd PID 77189, service matches install.
hermes cron status       # Live: “Gateway is running — cron jobs will fire automatically.”
```

`gateway install` writes the unit. It is not a guarantee the process is up on this boot. First-class boot should `status` (or `start`) after install.

`hermes pause` (no `cron`) is a **global emergency stop**: new cron dispatch, kanban dispatch, new gateway turns. In-flight work is not killed. This is not `dora harness pause`. Do not call it.

Laptop close is host sleep. The ticker stops. Due jobs may fire on wake if the job is still `[active]`. That matches spec stories 33–35. Hermes has no “pause because the lid closed.”

---

Local `hermes --help` lists ~70 top-level commands. Most are out of scope (pets, WhatsApp, claw, desktop). Keep this short list.

### Must keep wrapping

| Hermes | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `gateway install` + later `start`/`status` | Night ticker |
| `mcp add` + `mcp login` + `mcp test` | Scalekit URL + OAuth |
| `cron create` / `pause` / `resume` / `list` | Boot / pause / list |
| `-z` / `chat --oneshot` | Grill one-pass |

### Should wrap next (first-class holes)

| Hermes | Dora verb it would serve |
|--------|---------------------------|
| `mcp login scalekit` | After boot, or a dedicated `dora harness login` |
| `tools enable mcp-scalekit --platform cron` | So the night job can see Scalekit |

FileContent.content:
1→---
name: code-review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?
10→
Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.
20→
Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
30→2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

40→- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
50→- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

60→**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
70→- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

### 2. Identify the spec source

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
30→2. A path the user passed as an argument.

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

1→# Contributing to doraval

## Setup

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run dev -- --help    # run the CLI from source
```

10→Requires Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (see `engines` in `package.json`).

## Before you send a PR

```bash
bun test           # 615+ tests must pass
bun run typecheck  # baseline has pre-existing errors; don't add new ones
```

CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs `bun test` on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The matrix must be green.
20→
## Code philosophy

Read `AGENTS.md` first. It has the ponytail ladder (YAGNI → reuse → stdlib → installed deps → shortest form → minimum code) this codebase is written against. In short:

- Deletion and reuse beat new surface. Don't add an abstraction for one caller.
- Non-trivial logic gets one small test, not a suite.
- Never skip trust-boundary validation, data-loss error paths, or security handling.

## Commits
30→
Conventional Commits style (`fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`, `chore:`), matching `git log` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep the subject under ~70 chars; explain *why* in the body when it isn't obvious from the diff.

## Version bumps

Don't bump the version in a PR. Releases are cut by maintainers via `bun run bump` / `bun run release` (see `WIP.md` for current release status and policy).

## Filing issues

Prefer `dora report` from inside a project using doraval. It drafts a sanitized issue (no env values, no secrets) with the diagnostic payload maintainers need. Manual issues are fine too.
40→
## Website docs

Canonical user docs live in `apps/website/content/` (MDX). Pick one addressee per page: **Reader** (human: README, install, get-started) or **Runner** (the agent that executes `dora`: skill, per-command `--help`). Do not mix them. Terms match `CONTEXT.md`.

When writing or editing them:

1. Follow the style prompt in `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` (or load the `docs-writing-style` skill in review mode).
2. Prefer website MDX over `docs/developer-journey.md`. The journey file is product narrative with a command rename map at the top; it is not shipping user docs.
3. Open every page with 1–3 sentences of prose before the first code fence. Command pages need options, common mistakes, and related links.
50→
## Where things live

| Area | Path |
|---|---|
| CLI commands | `src/cli/commands/` |
| Core logic (review, fix, scaffold, memory) | `src/core/` |
| Provider specs (`dora skill new`, `dora plugin bump`) | `src/providers/` |
| Website / docs | `apps/website/` |
| Docs style prompt | `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` |
60→

1→# Doraval — agent conditions

## Before you write code (ponytail ladder)

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **YAGNI** — Does this need to exist? Speculative = skip, say so in one line.
2. **Reuse** — Already in this repo? Use it.
3. **Stdlib / Bun / platform** — Prefer built-ins over new helpers.
10→4. **Installed deps** — Use what is already in `package.json`. Never add a dep for a few lines.
5. **One line** — Prefer the shortest correct form.
6. **Only then** — Minimum code that works. Fewest files. Deletion > addition.

Never lazy about: trust-boundary validation, data-loss error paths, security, or understanding the full call path before editing.

Non-trivial logic leaves **one** small test. No version bumps unless the user asks for a release (see `WIP.md`).

## Skills

20→Look up project/system skills when deciding. Mention 1–2 options to the user when useful.

- CLI surfaces: `cli-developer`, `devrel-tooling`, `nodejs-cli-best-practices`
- Lean code: `ponytail`, `karpathy-guidelines`, `pragmatic-fp`
- Audits: `improve` (plans only — does not implement)
- Website docs: `docs-writing-style` + `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` (canonical user docs are `apps/website/content/`, not local journey notes)

## Feature release = docs lockstep

A user-visible feature is not released until the docs match the binary. CHANGELOG is not enough. Do not tag until these agree with the new behavior:
30→
- `apps/website/content/` (canonical Reader docs)
- README command catalog
- `skills/doraval/` (Runner: `SKILL.md` + `references/`)

Help text (`dora --help`, `dora --help --json`) is part of the product. If a new help line would disagree with README or `/commands`, update those pages in the same change.

## Release / npm platform packages (learned the hard way)

**Incident source:** Claude session `bdd5e085` (2026-07-08/09, B1 first ship) + commits `9389365`, recovery for v0.5.0–0.5.2. Same failure pattern on **v0.6.0**.
40→
### Symptom

CI `publish-npm` logs:

```
npm notice publish Signed provenance statement…   # only when --provenance is on
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@hacksmith%2fdoraval-darwin-arm64
```
50→
Main `@hacksmith/doraval` may still publish. Platform packages stay on an older version → **broken install**: optionalDeps point at missing binaries; stub says "platform package is not installed."

### Wrong diagnosis (do not repeat)

"Granular access token can't create new package names under the scope" — **disproven**. Same token published the packages successfully from a local shell.

### Confirmed diagnosis

- Failure is **auth/permissions on the five platform packages**, not a missing package-ACL list in the general sense.
60→- **`npm publish --access public` without `--provenance` from a local shell works** when the token can publish (or you pass `--otp=<code>` for 2FA).
- CI historically failed with `--provenance` on platforms (provenance signed, then PUT 404). CI was patched to drop provenance for platforms only (`9389365`); main still uses `--provenance`.
- **v0.6.0 recovery (2026-07-14):** whoami worked but publish returned **EOTP** until `npm publish --otp=…`. All five platforms published locally from GH release binaries. npm may return **E404** when the token lacks write/Bypass-2FA — do not misread that as "package missing."
- If platforms still 404/EOTP in CI, **do not ship main alone** and do not invent new version bumps — recover with the local procedure below. CI `NPM_TOKEN` should be a granular token with **write + Bypass 2FA** on all five platform packages (and main).

### Recovery procedure (when CI platform publish fails)

Do **not** bump the version. Reuse the release tag's binaries.

```bash
70→# 1) Download GitHub Release artifacts for the tag (e.g. v0.6.0)
TAG=v0.6.0
VERSION=${TAG#v}
SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/artifacts"
for f in doraval-darwin-arm64 doraval-darwin-x64 doraval-linux-x64 \
         doraval-linux-arm64 doraval-win32-x64.exe; do
  curl -fsSL "https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/releases/download/${TAG}/${f}" \
    -o "$SCRATCH/artifacts/${f}"
done
80→
# 2) Assemble platform packages (same as CI)
bun run scripts/platform-packages.ts "$VERSION" "$SCRATCH/artifacts" "$SCRATCH/platform-packages"

# 3) Publish EACH platform package LOCALLY — no --provenance
#    If EOTP: npm publish --access public --otp=XXXXXX  (or use a Bypass-2FA GAT)
for dir in "$SCRATCH/platform-packages"/*/; do
  (cd "$dir" && npm publish --access public ${OTP:+--otp="$OTP"})
done

90→# 4) Verify all five exist at $VERSION
for p in darwin-arm64 darwin-x64 linux-x64 linux-arm64 win32-x64; do
  npm view "@hacksmith/doraval-$p@$VERSION" version
done

# 5) Main package: only if missing for this version
#    bun run scripts/prepare-npm-publish.ts && npm publish --access public --provenance
#    then: git checkout -- package.json   # NEVER commit injected optionalDependencies
```

100→**Rules:**

- Never commit publish-time `optionalDependencies` injection (`prepare-npm-publish.ts` is CI-only).
- Never publish main until all five platform packages are on the registry (workflow is fail-fast; keep it that way).
- Prefer binaries from the **GitHub Release for that tag**, not a stale local smoke binary (session bug: mismatched darwin-arm64 content vs other arches).
- After recovery: verify with real install (`npm install @hacksmith/doraval@$VERSION` in a clean dir, then run `doraval --version`) — `npx` can hide optionalDep failures.

### Workflow file

`.github/workflows/release.yml` — platforms: `npm publish --access public` (no provenance); main: with provenance; fail-fast + registry check after each platform.
110→
## Product / agent docs (context only — do not derail the task)

- https://code.claude.com/llms.txt
- https://developers.openai.com/llms.txt
- https://docs.github.com/llms.txt
- https://cursor.com/docs/plugins
- https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated/openai-docs
- https://www.termcn.dev/llms.txt

120→## Resume

**Tracker:** `WIP.md` (only progress pin). See release status there for v0.6.0 npm platform gap.


Good Skill and Plugin references:
- https://github.com/nutlope/hallmark
- https://github.com/obra/superpowers

# Doraval — agent conditions

## Before you write code (ponytail ladder)

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **YAGNI** — Does this need to exist? Speculative = skip, say so in one line.
2. **Reuse** — Already in this repo? Use it.
3. **Stdlib / Bun / platform** — Prefer built-ins over new helpers.
4. **Installed deps** — Use what is already in `package.json`. Never add a dep for a few lines.
5. **One line** — Prefer the shortest correct form.
6. **Only then** — Minimum code that works. Fewest files. Deletion > addition.

Never lazy about: trust-boundary validation, data-loss error paths, security, or understanding the full call path before editing.

Non-trivial logic leaves **one** small test. No version bumps unless the user asks for a release (see `WIP.md`).

## Skills

Look up project/system skills when deciding. Mention 1–2 options to the user when useful.

- CLI surfaces: `cli-developer`, `devrel-tooling`, `nodejs-cli-best-practices`
- Lean code: `ponytail`, `karpathy-guidelines`, `pragmatic-fp`
- Audits: `improve` (plans only — does not implement)
- Website docs: `docs-writing-style` + `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` (canonical user docs are `apps/website/content/`, not local journey notes)

## Feature release = docs lockstep

A user-visible feature is not released until the docs match the binary. CHANGELOG is not enough. Do not tag until these agree with the new behavior:

- `apps/website/content/` (canonical Reader docs)
- README command catalog
- `skills/doraval/` (Runner: `SKILL.md` + `references/`)

Help text (`dora --help`, `dora --help --json`) is part of the product. If a new help line would disagree with README or `/commands`, update those pages in the same change.

## Release / npm platform packages (learned the hard way)

**Incident source:** Claude session `bdd5e085` (2026-07-08/09, B1 first ship) + commits `9389365`, recovery for v0.5.0–0.5.2. Same failure pattern on **v0.6.0**.

### Symptom

CI `publish-npm` logs:

```
npm notice publish Signed provenance statement…   # only when --provenance is on
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@hacksmith%2fdoraval-darwin-arm64
```

Main `@hacksmith/doraval` may still publish. Platform packages stay on an older version → **broken install**: optionalDeps point at missing binaries; stub says "platform package is not installed."

### Wrong diagnosis (do not repeat)

"Granular access token can't create new package names under the scope" — **disproven**. Same token published the packages successfully from a local shell.

### Confirmed diagnosis

- Failure is **auth/permissions on the five platform packages**, not a missing package-ACL list in the general sense.
- **`npm publish --access public` without `--provenance` from a local shell works** when the token can publish (or you pass `--otp=<code>` for 2FA).
- CI historically failed with `--provenance` on platforms (provenance signed, then PUT 404). CI was patched to drop provenance for platforms only (`9389365`); main still uses `--provenance`.
- **v0.6.0 recovery (2026-07-14):** whoami worked but publish returned **EOTP** until `npm publish --otp=…`. All five platforms published locally from GH release binaries. npm may return **E404** when the token lacks write/Bypass-2FA — do not misread that as "package missing."
- If platforms still 404/EOTP in CI, **do not ship main alone** and do not invent new version bumps — recover with the local procedure below. CI `NPM_TOKEN` should be a granular token with **write + Bypass 2FA** on all five platform packages (and main).

### Recovery procedure (when CI platform publish fails)

Do **not** bump the version. Reuse the release tag's binaries.

```bash
# 1) Download GitHub Release artifacts for the tag (e.g. v0.6.0)
TAG=v0.6.0
VERSION=${TAG#v}
SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/artifacts"
for f in doraval-darwin-arm64 doraval-darwin-x64 doraval-linux-x64 \
         doraval-linux-arm64 doraval-win32-x64.exe; do
  curl -fsSL "https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/releases/download/${TAG}/${f}" \
    -o "$SCRATCH/artifacts/${f}"
done

# 2) Assemble platform packages (same as CI)
bun run scripts/platform-packages.ts "$VERSION" "$SCRATCH/artifacts" "$SCRATCH/platform-packages"

# 3) Publish EACH platform package LOCALLY — no --provenance
#    If EOTP: npm publish --access public --otp=XXXXXX  (or use a Bypass-2FA GAT)
for dir in "$SCRATCH/platform-packages"/*/; do
  (cd "$dir" && npm publish --access public ${OTP:+--otp="$OTP"})
done

# 4) Verify all five exist at $VERSION
for p in darwin-arm64 darwin-x64 linux-x64 linux-arm64 win32-x64; do
  npm view "@hacksmith/doraval-$p@$VERSION" version
done

# 5) Main package: only if missing for this version
#    bun run scripts/prepare-npm-publish.ts && npm publish --access public --provenance
#    then: git checkout -- package.json   # NEVER commit injected optionalDependencies
```

**Rules:**

- Never commit publish-time `optionalDependencies` injection (`prepare-npm-publish.ts` is CI-only).
- Never publish main until all five platform packages are on the registry (workflow is fail-fast; keep it that way).
- Prefer binaries from the **GitHub Release for that tag**, not a stale local smoke binary (session bug: mismatched darwin-arm64 content vs other arches).
- After recovery: verify with real install (`npm install @hacksmith/doraval@$VERSION` in a clean dir, then run `doraval --version`) — `npx` can hide optionalDep failures.

### Workflow file

`.github/workflows/release.yml` — platforms: `npm publish --access public` (no provenance); main: with provenance; fail-fast + registry check after each platform.

1→# Local use-case runner

Date: 2026-08-31
Status: ready-for-agent
Source: [wayfinder map](map.md)

## Post-spec change (2026-08-31)

The grill skill lives in **doraval** (`skills/`).
10→It does not live in the kit.
`dora harness new` starts it.

## Tickets

- [#79](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/79) Harness group on the closed tree
- [#80](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/80) Routine folder + list + open (blocked by #79)
- [#81](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/81) Grill skill + `dora harness new` (blocked by #80)
- [#82](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/82) Boot, pause, resume (blocked by #80)
- [#83](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/83) Docs lockstep (blocked by #81 and #82)
20→
Frontier: #79. Next session: `/implement` #79. Clear context between tickets.

## Problem Statement

An internal Scalekit teammate wants a use case to keep running after the chat closes.

They already have LLM credits. They can paste a Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL. They do not want a new CLI. They do not want a shared team bot. They do not want Slack, Discord, or Webflow baked into the runner.

Today they can grill a use case in a chat. Then the chat ends. Nothing runs on an interval. Tokens and tools are not wired for a night pass. There is no saved object they can pause or boot again.
30→
## Solution

The teammate opens **Dora**. Dora is the front desk.

A **grill skill** (authored in this kit) turns a use case into a **routine**. A routine is a saved folder at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. It is the only product object.

Dora then helps run that prompt **once**. After that one pass, `dora harness boot` starts **Hermes** only: the Hermes gateway as a machine service, plus one Hermes cron job. Dora exits. Hermes runs a **loop**: the same prompt, on an interval.

Tools go through **Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP**. Slack, Discord, and Webflow are connectors on a use case. They are not part of the harness.
40→
The teammate brings their own LLM credits. This spec describes the product. It does not install it.

## User Stories

1. As an internal Scalekit teammate, I want to open Dora rather than Hermes, so that I have one front desk for create, boot, pause, and list.
2. As a teammate, I want use-case verbs under `dora harness`, so that I do not mix them with `dora review`.
3. As a teammate, I want `dora harness new` to start the grill skill, so that I do not write a routine by hand.
4. As a teammate, I want the grill to ask what the use case does, so that the unattended prompt is specific.
5. As a teammate, I want the grill to collect skills to **run**, skills to **refer to**, and the Scalekit Agent Gateway URL, so that a night pass has what it needs.
50→6. As a teammate, I want a default shared MCP URL that I paste once, so that I do not paste it for every routine.
7. As a teammate, I want a routine to override that URL, so that one odd job can use a different gateway.
8. As a teammate, I want the grill to pick a slug I can read, so that I can type `dora harness boot ooo-calendar`.
9. As a teammate, I want to rename the slug, so that a bad first name is not permanent.
10. As an agent running the grill, I want to mirror `grill-with-docs` (interview plus a paper trail), so that answers are not lost in chat.
11. As an agent running the grill, I want `writing-for-agents` to write the full unattended prompt after the interview, so that the night text is written for an agent, not a human chat.
12. As a teammate, I want one live test pass before anything is scheduled, so that a bad prompt does not run every hour.
13. As a teammate, I want Dora to print the one-pass command, so that I can run it myself.
14. As a teammate, I want Dora to offer an interactive flow for that one pass, so that I do not have to copy a command if I do not want to.
15. As a teammate without Hermes, I want Dora to print official Hermes install steps plus the command, so that I know what to install. I do not want Dora to install Hermes.
60→16. As a teammate without Hermes, I want Dora to refuse to fake a test run, so that I am not told it worked when it did not.
17. As a teammate, I want Dora to write the routine folder only after the one pass is done (or I accept the printed command path), so that disk does not hold a scheduled job I never saw.
18. As a teammate, I want a routine to live at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`, so that I know where it is.
19. As a teammate, I want the routine to hold the prompt, skill directories, MCP URL, interval, and max tick, so that boot has one source.
20. As a teammate, I want the default interval to be every 1 hour, so that I do not set a schedule for a first job.
21. As a teammate, I want the default max tick to be 10 minutes, so that one stuck pass cannot run forever.
22. As a teammate, I want both fields to be configurable per routine, so that a tight job can run more often.
23. As a teammate, I want `dora harness boot <slug>` to start that routine, so that I do not touch Hermes cron by hand.
24. As a teammate, I want bare `dora harness boot` to list existing routines and let me pick one or create, so that I do not have to remember slugs.
25. As a teammate, I want boot to start the Hermes gateway as a machine service, so that the loop keeps ticking after Dora exits.
70→26. As a teammate, I want boot to write one Hermes cron job from the routine, so that Hermes owns the timer.
27. As a teammate, I want Dora to exit after boot, so that I can close that terminal.
28. As a teammate, I want another terminal to work for pause and list, so that I do not attach to the first session.
29. As a teammate, I want `dora harness pause <slug>` to pause that cron job only, so that other routines on the same gateway keep running.
30. As a teammate, I want pause to leave the gateway up, so that I do not kill every loop to stop one.
31. As a teammate, I want a pause to mean “skip later ticks,” so that a pass that already started may finish.
32. As a teammate, I want `dora harness resume <slug>` to start later ticks again, so that pause is reversible.
33. As a teammate, I want closing the laptop to be sleep, not pause, so that I do not think I paused when the clock just stopped.
34. As a teammate, I want to know that cron does not run while the host sleeps, so that I do not expect night work from a closed Mac.
35. As a teammate, I want due jobs to be able to fire on wake if they are not paused, so that I understand what happens after I open the lid.
80→36. As a teammate, I want `dora harness list` to show routines and whether each job is running or paused, so that I can see state.
37. As a teammate, I want `dora harness open <slug>` to open that routine folder, so that I can read or edit the prompt.
38. As a teammate, I want the first MCP connect to be Hermes OAuth / magic link, so that Scalekit can store provider tokens.
39. As a teammate, I want Dora to stay off that magic link, so that Dora does not sit in the OAuth path.
40. As a teammate, I want night runs to reuse `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/` after one login, so that I am not at the keyboard every hour.
41. As a teammate, I want a refresh failure to stop and ask me to run `hermes mcp login`, so that a dead token does not look like a silent success.
42. As a teammate, I want a dead Scalekit connected account to stop and ask me to open the link again, so that I can fix the provider side.
43. As a teammate, I want the cron job toolset to include `mcp-<server>`, so that Scalekit tools are actually on the night pass.
44. As a teammate, I want Slack, Discord, and Webflow to be optional connectors on a use case, so that the harness does not assume Slack.
45. As a teammate, I want a loop to mean “same prompt on an interval,” so that I do not confuse it with polling one chat app.
90→46. As a teammate, I want to bring my own LLM credits, so that the runner does not sell inference.
47. As a teammate, I want skill directories to be pluggable, so that I can point at the skills this job needs.
48. As a teammate, I do not want skillkit to be the default, so that a laptop without skillkit still works.
49. As a teammate, I want an optional later copy of a routine into skillkit, so that sharing is possible without being required.
50. As a teammate, I want an optional later way to point Dora at a repo of routines, so that a team folder can land later.
51. As a teammate, I want optional `dora review` on attached skill directories, so that I can check those skills if I want. The product must work if I skip that review.
52. As a teammate, I want secrets kept off git, so that an optional remote does not leak tokens.
53. As a teammate, I want an optional git remote on the routine folder later, so that I can share the prompt and not the secrets.
54. As a teammate, I want Hermes to be the only runtime in this spec, so that I do not get a Claude / Grok / OpenCode runner in v1.
55. As a teammate, I want missing Hermes to print install steps and stop on boot too, so that boot does not fail in a cryptic way.
100→56. As a doraval maintainer, I want the grill skill in `skills/` and shipped only after `dora review --quick` exits 0, so that a draft does not land in the catalog.
57. As a doraval maintainer, I want the grill skill to follow writing-for-agents (imperative, no “You are,” no em-dashes), so that the night text is written for an agent.
58. As a doraval maintainer, I want the shipped Doraval skill catalog to name `dora harness` when the group ships, so that the Runner map does not lie.
59. As a doraval maintainer, I want `harness` added as a core command group (`defineGroup`), so that the verbs are real CLI, not a plugin.
60. As a doraval maintainer, I want root verbs like `dora review` unchanged, so that existing Dora users are not moved.
61. As a first reader, I want the spec, docs, and grill wording to talk to an internal teammate, so that I am not sold a customer product yet.
62. As a later reader, I want a path that is not locked to Scalekit customers only (anyone with Dora, Hermes, and an MCP URL), so that opening up later does not require a rewrite of the objects. This spec does not write that later wording.
63. As a teammate, I want one machine and one user, so that I do not need a company fleet setup.
64. As a teammate, I want no first sample use case forced by this spec, so that the harness stays generic.

110→## Implementation Decisions

- One repo plus one runtime. Doraval authors the grill skill under `skills/` and grows the `dora harness` group. Hermes is configured, not forked. The kit does not own this work.
- The user-facing object is a **routine**. Hermes still stores a cron **job**. The teammate hears “routine.”
- Routine path: `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. Slug comes from the grill and may be renamed. Commands take the slug.
- Routine contents (contract, not file names): unattended prompt, skill directories to run, skill directories to refer to, MCP URL, interval, max tick. The shape is extensible. Secrets do not live in a file that an optional git remote would publish.
- Default schedule: every 1 hour. Default max tick: 10 minutes (Hermes 600s). Both are per-routine and may be changed later by the grill or by `dora harness`.
- `dora harness` verbs: `new`, `boot`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, `open`. `resume` is required because pause must reverse. `open` opens the routine folder.
- Bare `boot` lists routines and lets the teammate pick one or start create (same path as `new`). `boot <slug>` boots that routine.
- Boot sequence: if Hermes is missing, print official install steps and stop. If Hermes is present, ensure the gateway is running as a machine service, write one cron job from the routine (toolset includes `mcp-<server>`), then exit. Dora does not own a timer.
120→- Pause calls `hermes cron pause` for that job. Job state becomes `paused`. Gateway stays up. A running pass may finish. Resume calls `hermes cron resume`.
- Laptop close is host sleep. Official Hermes: cron does not run while the host sleeps. Sleep is not pause.
- Scalekit is a normal HTTP MCP server in Hermes (`url` plus `auth: oauth`). It is not the Nous Tool Gateway. The teammate pastes the MCP URL. Dora does not mint Virtual MCP session tokens with API keys.
- First connect is Hermes OAuth / magic link. Scalekit stores provider tokens. Hermes stores MCP login under `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/`. Later ticks reuse those files. Refresh is automatic while the refresh token is valid.
- Refresh fail or missing cache: stop and tell the human to run `hermes mcp login <server>`. A dead connected account: stop and tell the human to open the provider link again. Cron has no TTY. Do not pretend a browser flow will work at night.
- Grill skill: we author it in doraval under `skills/`. Ship with `dora review --quick` on that skill directory. Do not draft it in the kit. Do not update kit `ask-saif`.
- Grill shape: mirror `grill-with-docs`. Pragmatic gate before save: skills to run, skills to refer to, Scalekit Agent Gateway URL. Then `writing-for-agents` writes the unattended prompt. Then one test pass (print the command, or an interactive flow). Then write the routine folder.
- Later, steal Warp skill-doctor checks that fit. Those checks are not a v1 gate.
- Dora may later copy a routine to skillkit, or point at a repo of routines. Not required for v1.
- Optional `dora review` on attached skill directories. Skip is fine.
130→- User brings LLM credits. This spec does not provision a model key.
- Do not write loop product terms into kit `CONTEXT.md`. Kit glossary stays the language of the kit.
- First wording is for an internal teammate. Do not pick a first sample use case.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate can see or what Dora writes. It does not check Hermes internals. It does not start a live gateway in CI. It does not run a real Scalekit OAuth dance.

### Seams

140→1. **Primary seam: `dora harness` CLI (doraval).** Assert help text, missing-Hermes install steps, routine folder write, and the Hermes commands Dora would run for boot, pause, resume, and list. Prefer doraval’s existing command-tree / CLI tests.
2. **Secondary seam: grill skill in doraval `skills/`.** Assert `dora review <skill-dir> --quick` exits 0. Also assert the skill names the pragmatic gate and the one-pass-then-save order. Do not automate the interview.
3. **Shared artifact: routine folder contract.** The folder is the seam between Dora and Hermes. Assert slug, prompt, skill dirs, MCP URL, interval, and max tick are present. Do not assert Hermes job JSON schema beyond what Dora is specified to write.

### Modules under test

- Doraval `harness` group (behavior at the CLI).
- Grill skill (review plus the documented gate and order).
- Routine folder writer (contract above).

150→### Prior art

- Doraval: `dora review --quick` on the grill skill. Closed command tree plus CLI tests for each verb. New group follows that pattern.
- No Hermes test double that reimplements cron.

## Out of Scope

- A new CLI beside Dora.
- Hermes Tool Gateway as the Slack (or any connector) path.
- Minting Scalekit session tokens with API keys (Virtual MCP mint path).
160→- Claude, Grok, or OpenCode as the runtime in this spec.
- The whole product as “a kit skill.” The grill skill lives in doraval. The runner is still Dora plus Hermes.
- Picking a first sample use case (Discord, GitHub, or OOO). The spec stays generic.
- Wording and docs for “anyone with the stack.” First reader is an internal teammate.
- Company setup on more than one machine.
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Dora sitting on the magic link / OAuth path.
- Push, webhooks, or a Hermes Slack bot. The interval is the trigger.
- Making skillkit the default skill directory.
- Writing loop terms into kit `CONTEXT.md`. Doraval `CONTEXT.md` may gain routine / harness / loop terms when the group ships.
170→- Shipping the grill skill in this spec session. Spec first. Tickets next.

## Further Notes

Map: [Local use cases](map.md).

Research:

- Loop runners survey: `docs/research/2026-08-28-always-on-loop-runners.md`
- Hermes cron and MCP OAuth: `docs/research/2026-08-29-hermes-cron-mcp-oauth.md`
180→- Dora command growth: `docs/research/2026-08-29-dora-command-extension.md`

Next skill after this spec is accepted: `/to-tickets`. Then `/implement` per ticket in a fresh session.

Hermes is not installed on the author’s machine yet. A live one-pass test waits until a human installs it. That install is a later `/wizard` or a human step. It is not this spec.

1→---
name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

10→When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

20→A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

When the shape of that interface is itself in question — how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose — use the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

30→- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

When the shape of that interface is itself in question — how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose — use the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.
